summary: This program asks for a temperature in Celsius, converts it to Fahrenheit, and prints the result. If what you type is not a number, it catches the NumberFormatException and prints a friendly message instead of crashing.

lines.text: Using print rather than println leaves the cursor on the same line, so the reader types the answer right after the prompt.
This is a try-with-resources block: the Scanner is created here and closed automatically when the block ends, however it ends. Everything inside is also guarded by the catch clauses below.
The typed line is stripped of stray spaces by trim and then converted to a number. Double.parseDouble is the line that throws NumberFormatException when the text is not a valid number.
The conversion itself lives in its own method, so main stays focused on talking to the user.
This catch handles the one failure the program can genuinely predict: input that is not numeric. Because it is listed first, it takes priority over the broader catch below.

A safety net for anything else that could go wrong, such as no input being available at all. A general catch must always come after the more specific ones, or the compiler will reject it as unreachable.
A small static method with a clear name and a single job, which is what makes it easy to reuse and to test.
Multiplying by 9 before dividing by 5 matters here: celsius is a double, so the arithmetic stays in decimals rather than truncating the way 9/5 alone would with whole numbers.
